q: According to KOC.SA.002, how often must an in-service scaffold be re-inspected by an authorized Scaffolding Inspector, whether or not it has been used?
options: Only after alterations or bad weather
source: Cl. 4.1.3 / 5.1.6: inspection before first use, after alteration, after adverse weather and every 7 days thereafter.

q: Above what wind speed does KOC.SA.002 prohibit work on or from scaffolds?
source: Cl. 5.1.3 c): work on scaffolds is prohibited during storms or high winds (wind speed more than 65 km/h).

q: An elevated scaffold work area requires at least two means of exit when the horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit ladder exceeds:
source: Cl. 5.1.3 f): where horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit exceeds 15 m (50 ft), at least two means of exit are required.

q: A worker is setting up a portable ladder against a structure. Which set-up ratio meets the KOC.SA.002 requirement of approximately 76 degrees?
options: 1 m out for every 2 m up
1 m out for every 3 m up
1 m out for every 4 m up
1 m out for every 6 m up
source: Cl. 5.2.2 h): ladders shall be set at an angle of 76 degrees (1 m out for 4 m up).

q: Where no adequate handhold is provided at the landing, a portable ladder must extend above the landing place by at least:
source: Cl. 5.2.2 i): the ladder must rise at least 1.05 m (3.5 ft) above the landing place.

q: Without a supporting risk assessment, what is the minimum distance a scaffold may be erected from an existing excavation?
source: Cl. 5.1.3 aa): no scaffold shall be erected less than 3 m from an existing excavation; a shorter distance only based on a risk assessment.

q: What minimum experience does KOC.SA.002 require for a Scaffolding Supervisor, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
options: 3 years in scaffolding, with no supervisory requirement
5 years in scaffolding, including at least 1 year as a supervisor
5 years in scaffolding, including at least 3 years as a supervisor
10 years in scaffolding, including at least 2 years as a supervisor
source: Cl. 5.1.2 b): minimum 5 years' experience in scaffolding jobs, of which at least one year in a supervisory role.

q: What is the maximum permitted height of a portable stepladder under KOC.SA.002?
source: Cl. 5.2.3 f): portable stepladders shall not exceed 20 ft (6.1 m) in height.

q: A scaffold has been inspected and certified safe for use. What colour Scaffolding Tag should be displayed at its access points?
source: Cl. 4.1.5 / 5.1.6: scaffolds certified safe for use carry a Green Scaffolding Tag; incomplete or unsafe scaffolds carry a Red tag.

q: A worker finds that the Scaffolding Tag holder at a scaffold access point is empty. What does this mean?
options: The scaffold shall not be used
The scaffold is due for its 7-day inspection
The tag is being re-printed and work may continue
The scaffold is safe for light duty only
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.1.6: an empty Scaffolding Tag holder denotes that the scaffold shall not be used.

q: In addition to the required diploma or science degree, what minimum scaffolding experience must a Scaffold Inspector have?
source: Cl. 5.1.2 a): Scaffold Inspector — diploma (Engineering) or science graduate with five (5) years' experience in scaffold erection, modification and disassembly.

q: What minimum experience is required for a Scaffolder, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
source: Cl. 5.1.2 c): Scaffolders shall have certified training and three (3) years' experience in the related field.

q: How should scaffold components be brought down from height during dismantling?
options: Dropped onto a heap of sand below
Thrown into a barricaded drop zone
Slid down a ladder used as a chute
Lowered hand to hand or by gin wheel
source: Cl. 5.1.1 c): scaffold materials shall not be thrown or dropped; they shall be raised or lowered hand to hand or by crane, gin wheel or other suitable means.

q: What certification does KOC.SA.002 require for a gin wheel used on site to raise scaffold materials?
options: No certification if load is under 50 kg
Visual check by the Scaffolder only
source: Cl. 5.1.1 c): gin wheel used at site shall be third party certified; the worksite supervisor ensures wheel and rope are in good condition.

q: Which of the following shall NOT be used as a means of access to a scaffold platform?
source: Cl. 5.1.3 g): portable or attached ladders, stair towers, ramps etc. shall be used; cross braces shall not be used as a means of access.

q: When must scaffold ties be fixed during erection?
options: Only when the scaffold is complete
source: Cl. 5.1.3 l): ties shall be fixed as erection proceeds, not when the scaffold is complete.

q: How many scaffold erection, modification or dismantling jobs may one Scaffolding Supervisor supervise at the same time?
options: As many as are on the same site
source: Cl. 5.1.3 z): a Scaffolding Supervisor can supervise only one scaffold erection, modification or dismantling job at any given time.

q: Materials must not be stored on or under a scaffold. At what minimum distance from the scaffold area should they be stored?
source: Cl. 5.1.6: no materials shall be stored over or under the scaffold; materials shall be stored 3 m away from the scaffold erected area.

q: Rejected scaffold materials must be removed from project sites within how many working days?
source: Cl. 4.1.7: Controlling Team shall ensure all rejected materials are removed from project sites within fifteen (15) working days.

q: How many persons may be on a portable ladder at any one time?
source: Cl. 5.2.2 s): only one person shall be on the ladder at any one time.

q: When working from a portable ladder, the working position shall be no higher than how many rungs from the top?
source: Cl. 5.2.2 t): the working position shall not be less than five rungs from the top of the ladder.

q: What is the maximum validity of a Hot, Cold or Radiography Work Permit from its date of issue, subject to renewal by the Permit Issuer?
source: Cl. 5.4: Hot / Cold / Radiography permits are valid for a maximum of seven consecutive days from the date of issue, subject to renewal.

q: A Work Permit endorsement or renewal remains valid for a maximum of:
source: Cl. 5.8 e): each endorsement / renewal is valid for a maximum of one shift (12 hours) or as recorded by the Permit Issuer.

q: A worksite was gas tested and certified gas free at 07:00, but the job could not start until 09:30. What must happen before work starts?
options: Work may start because the certificate is valid for the shift
Work may start if the Worksite Supervisor signs the permit
A new gas test must be carried out
Work may start if a fire watch is posted
source: Cl. 5.15 b): if work has not started within 2 hours of a gas test, the gas free certification becomes invalid and a new test is required.

q: What is the maximum flammable gas reading permitted for authorizing Hot Work under the KOC Permit to Work Procedure?
source: Cl. 5.13.2 / 5.15 g): the maximum LEL permissible for authorized Hot Work is 0% LEL.

q: During cold work on a flowline, 0% LEL cannot be achieved despite depressurizing, venting and purging. Under what condition may the work proceed?
options: Below 10% LEL, continuously monitored, with an approved Method Statement
Below 20% LEL, with all workers wearing breathing apparatus sets
Below 25% LEL, with a fire watch and extinguishers posted at site
Any LEL reading, with verbal approval from the Permit Issuer
source: Cl. 5.13.1 c): work may be carried out ensuring LEL does not exceed 10% under continuous monitoring; a reviewed and approved Method Statement is mandatory.

q: What is the maximum period a Work Permit can remain suspended before it must be cancelled and signed off?
options: 24 hours, after which it is cancelled
3 days, after which it is cancelled
5 days, or permit expiry if sooner
source: Cl. 5.11: a Work Permit can be suspended for a maximum of 5 days or until expiry of its validity, whichever is sooner.

q: What is the minimum fire extinguisher provision for each Hot Work location under KOC.SA.004?
source: Cl. 5.16 a): a minimum of two fire extinguishers (9 kg Monnex or 12 kg DCP) within 7.5 m of each hot work location.

q: Unless otherwise stated in the permit, how long is an Excavation Notification valid from the date the Asset Owner signs it?
source: Cl. 5.13.6 e): the Excavation Notification is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.

q: What is the minimum passing score for the PTW qualifying written test for Permit Issuers, Permit Applicants and Worksite Supervisors?
source: Cl. 5.7 b): the passing score for the PTW qualifying test shall be a minimum of 70%.

q: Under KOC.SA.004, mechanical excavation is NOT allowed within what radius of any underground facility?
source: Cl. 5.13.6 a): mechanical excavation is not allowed inside the plant or facility or within 5 m radius of any underground facilities.

q: Under the KOC Permit to Work system, which of the following is a CERTIFICATE rather than a work permit?
source: Cl. 5.3: the PTW system has four types of Work Permits (Cold, Hot, Radiography, Vehicle/Mobile Equipment Entry) and one Certificate (Confined Space Entry).

q: Who authorizes (issues) a Work Permit for work in an operating area?
options: Permit Issuer of the Asset Operating Team
Safety Officer of the Asset HSE Team
Permit Applicant of the Controlling Team
source: Cl. 2.0 / 4.2: the Permit Issuer represents the Asset Operating Team in whose area of control the work is carried out.

q: How long is a Vehicle Entry Permit valid for a vehicle entering a hazardous area?
source: Cl. 5.4 / 5.13.5: Vehicle Entry Permit valid for one continuous shift; Mobile Equipment Entry valid up to 7 consecutive days.

q: Which of the following activities is listed as Critical Work in KOC.SA.004?
options: Working at a height of 1.5 metres
Heavy lifting of more than 50 tons
Cold work on a 220 V lighting circuit
source: Cl. 2.0 Critical Work examples: work at height > 1.8 m, excavation > 1.2 m, HV > 440 V, heavy lifting > 50 tons, etc.

q: How often must the PTW Authorization Card be revalidated after refresher training?
options: Every 2 years, or contract period if earlier
Every 3 years, or on change of job
Every year, regardless of contract period
Every 5 years, at the HSE Induction Center
source: Cl. 5.7 e): revalidated on expiry — every 2 years or contract period, whichever is earlier — after refresher training.

q: A contractor's Worksite Supervisor fails the PTW qualifying test. When may he re-appear for the test?
options: The next day, without any approval needed
After 1 month, with HSE Group approval
After 1 week, with Controlling Team approval
After 6 months, with Asset Owner approval
source: Cl. 5.7 f): he can re-appear after 1 week from the date of the last test with approval of the Controlling Team.

q: A mistake is made while filling a manual Work Permit. How must it be corrected?
options: Page torn out and a fresh copy started by the PI
Single line through it, initialled by PA and PI
Wrong entry overwritten neatly in ink by the PA
Correction fluid applied, then the entry rewritten
source: Cl. 5.8 b): mistakes crossed out with a single line and initialled by PA and PI; overwriting or correction fluid invalidates the permit.

q: In an emergency with actual or potential loss of life, how may urgent safety work begin without a Work Permit?
options: Verbal OK from PI or senior KOC person, logged
Not possible without a written permit
Verbal OK from any contractor supervisor
Only after a printed e-WP is issued
source: Cl. 5.1 d): PI or senior-most KOC personnel may verbally allow the work; recorded in the Operation Logbook and signed by the PI; permit prepared as soon as practical.

q: Before radiography starts, when are the Public Address (PA) announcements made?
options: Only at the moment radiography starts
source: Cl. 5.13.3 f): PA announcement 30 minutes prior and a further announcement 5 minutes prior to radiography commencement.

q: For Hot Work in a hazardous area, what minimum reach must the pressurized 2½-inch fire water hose have?
source: Cl. 5.16 b): a 2½" pressurized water hose capable of reaching a minimum distance of 30 m from the hot work location.

q: How many Fire Team-approved fire extinguishers must mobile equipment such as a welding machine have to enter a hazardous area?
source: Cl. 5.13.5 b): mobile equipment must have at least two fire extinguishers duly approved by Fire Team.

q: For which excavations is an Excavation Notification required under KOC.SA.004?
source: Cl. 5.13.6: an Excavation Notification is required for all excavations regardless of the depth.

q: A NORM survey before vessel cleaning gives a dose rate of 4 µSv/hr. How is the location classified?
source: Cl. 5.23: 0.5–10 µSv/hr = Supervised Area (hourly readings); above 10 µSv/hr = Controlled Area and work stopped.

q: During a routine check, an SCBA breathing air cylinder gauge shows it has dropped below full charge. At what point does KOC.SA.005 require it to be sent for recharging?
options: When pressure falls to 90% of the specified pressure
When pressure falls to 75% of the specified pressure
When pressure falls to 50% of the specified pressure
source: Cl. 4.2 / 5.4.3: cylinder pressure must not be less than 90% of full capacity; refill when pressure drops to 90% of specified pressure.

q: When checking an SCBA, the cylinder valve is closed slowly to test the low-pressure warning alarm. At approximately what level of cylinder capacity should the alarm sound?
source: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify activation of the low pressure alarm (to sound at approximately 25% of cylinder capacity).

q: What is the maximum validity of an RPE 'Authorized User Card' issued by the Controlling Team?
source: Cl. 5.4.4: validity of the Authorized User Card shall not exceed 12 months and must be within the medical examination validity.

q: What periodic hydrostatic test intervals does KOC.SA.005 specify for SCBA breathing air cylinders?
options: Steel every 3 years; composite every 5 years
Steel every 5 years; composite every 3 years
Steel and composite both every 5 years
Steel and composite both every 10 years
source: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify SCBA cylinder is current on hydrostatic test (5 years for steel, 3 years for composite cylinders).

q: A worker passes a quantitative fit test with a full-face respirator. Which requirement then applies on the job?
options: Any model from the same manufacturer may be used
Any size of the same model may be used
The exact same make, model, style and size must be used
Any tight-fitting respirator with the same APF may be used
source: Cl. 5.7: after passing a fit test, the user must use the exact same make, model, style and size of respirator; fit testing is at least annual.

q: What minimum specification does KOC.SA.005 set for SCBA used by emergency services (Fire Group)?
options: Negative pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 45 minutes duration
Positive pressure type, minimum 60 minutes duration
source: Cl. 5.2.1 Note 1: SCBA for emergency services shall be positive pressure type with minimum 45 minutes duration, conforming to NFPA 1981.

q: An air-purifying respirator filter has been removed from its sealed packaging but rarely used. When must it be replaced, regardless of use?
source: Cl. 5.4.5 B: a filter once opened from the seal must be replaced after 6 months regardless of its use.

q: How often, at a minimum, must the output air quality of a breathing air compressor be checked?
options: Every month, and after each filter change
Every 3 months, and after each filter change
Every 6 months, and after each filter change
Every 12 months, and after each filter change
source: Cl. 5.9: periodic checks of compressor output air quality at least once every 3 months and after each filter change.

q: For KOC.SA.005, an atmosphere is oxygen deficient (and treated as IDLH) when oxygen is below:
source: Cl. 2.0: oxygen deficient atmosphere — less than 19.5% oxygen by volume; treated as IDLH for this procedure.

q: What must a wearer of a tight-fitting respirator do to ensure an adequate face seal?
options: Apply barrier cream to the face
Wear a cap under the head straps
Be clean shaven where the mask seals
source: Cl. 4.6: all tight-fitting respirator wearers shall, according to manufacturer's instructions, be clean shaven.

q: Excluding escape-only sets, what is the minimum number of SCBA wearers that must be present when SCBA is used for work?
source: Cl. 4.6: SCBA/SAR users shall ensure a minimum of two SCBA wearers are present, with standby crew and an SCBA Controller.

q: For what purpose may an escape-only respirator be used?
source: Cl. 5.4.5: escape-only respirators must not be used for re-entry or work; they are for emergency exit only.

q: A quantitative fit test gives a fit factor of 100. What does this mean?
options: The mask is rated for use up to 100 ppm
The mask lets in 100% of the outside air
The mask may be worn for 100 minutes
Air inside is 100 times cleaner than outside
source: Cl. 2.0 Note: a fit factor of 100 means that the air inside the respirator is 100 times cleaner than the air outside.

q: How often must respirators maintained for emergency use be inspected by the Fire (Support Services) Team?
source: Cl. 5.4.5 table: respirators for emergency situations — at least monthly and checked before and after each use.

q: During inspection, the foil seal of an air-purifying escape respirator (APER) is found broken. What must be done?
options: Reseal the pouch with tape and keep it
Take it out of service and dispose of it
Return it to stock after a visual check
Use it for training sessions only
source: Cl. 5.4.5 A: if the foil seal has been broken, the APER must be taken out of service and disposed of.

q: What is the normal duration of an escape-only respirator as defined in KOC.SA.005?
source: Cl. 2.0: escape-only respirator — SCBA or APER type, normally 15 minutes duration.

q: How should an SCBA set be stored when not in use?
options: Cylinder valve closed, harness straps fully extended
Cylinder valve open, straps fully tightened
Facepiece fitted to the regulator under pressure
Cylinder partly charged to reduce stress
source: Cl. 5.4.3: SCBA stored with cylinder valves closed; harness straps adjusted to maximum length; cylinders stored fully charged.

q: Under the breathing air quality limits in KOC.SA.005 (NFPA 1989), the maximum carbon monoxide content is:
source: Cl. 5.9 table: carbon monoxide up to 5 ppm; CO2 up to 1000 ppm; oxygen 19.5–23.5%.

q: How often must RPE authorized users attend refresher training?
options: Only when the card is lost
source: Cl. 5.4.4: training must recur at least annually; RPE wearers shall undergo refresher training annually.

q: What minimum percentage of third-party SCBA inspection and servicing must be witnessed or verified by the Controlling Team?
source: Cl. 4.1 / 4.2: at least 5% of inspection / servicing by third parties shall be witnessed / verified by the Controlling Team.

q: What distinguishes a positive pressure respirator under KOC.SA.005?
options: Air is drawn through a filter cartridge
Facepiece pressure goes negative on inhalation
It is designed for escape use only
source: Cl. 2.0: positive pressure respirator — pressure inside the facepiece is positive during both inhalation and exhalation.

q: Which set of gas test results permits confined space entry WITHOUT respiratory protection under KOC.SA.007 Table 1?
source: Table 1: entry without respiratory protection when O2 is 19.5–23.5%, flammables < 10% LEL and H2S < 10 ppm.

q: Gas testing of a vessel shows 15% oxygen. According to KOC.SA.007 Table 1, what is the correct action?
options: Entry permitted with an air-purifying respirator
Entry permitted with forced ventilation only
Entry permitted with SCBA and continuous monitoring
No entry, except in an emergency or for rescue
source: Table 1: oxygen content less than 16% (or H2S > 100 ppm, or flammables 50% LEL or above) = NO ENTRY except emergency or rescue.

q: The initial confined space gas test was done at 08:00 but entry is delayed until 09:15. What does KOC.SA.007 require?
options: Entry may proceed because the test is valid for the shift
A follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor before entry
A new Confined Space Entry Certificate must be raised
Entry may proceed if entrants wear personal H2S monitors
source: Cl. 5.3: entry is to take place within one hour of the initial gas test; otherwise a follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor is required before entry.

q: Where periodic (rather than continuous) gas monitoring is used during a confined space entry, the interval between tests shall not exceed:
source: Cl. 5.13: the periodic monitoring of gas shall not exceed a two-hour period.

q: How frequently does KOC.SA.007 require personnel working inside a vessel or tank to be given a rest period, unless conditions require more frequent breaks?
source: Cl. 5.11: personnel working inside the vessel / tank will be given a rest period at each 30 minute interval, or more frequently.

q: Inside a KOC hydrocarbon facility, an excavation is classified as a confined space when its depth exceeds:
source: Cl. 2.0 c): excavation with depth more than 1.2 m inside hydrocarbon facilities is a confined space.

q: An entrant collapses inside a vessel. What is the correct immediate action for the standby person who is not trained in search and rescue?
options: Enter at once wearing an escape set and pull the entrant out
Summon aid via the Control Room and stay outside until relief arrives
Send another entrant inside to assist the casualty to the manway
Lower a spare SCBA set to the casualty and wait at the manway
source: Cl. 4.4 Note / 5.11: the standby person must not enter until relief arrives; he must summon aid immediately via the Control Room.

q: Which of the following must NEVER be used to ventilate a confined space?
source: Cl. 5.5: compressed oxygen or instrument air shall never be used to ventilate a confined space.

q: A vessel has been certified gas free but flammable residues may remain. If extra-low-voltage portable lighting is used, what is its maximum voltage under KOC.SA.007?
source: Cl. 5.6: such spaces may be illuminated by extra low voltage (25 V AC) portable lighting approved for Zone 1; transformers never taken inside.

q: When is a person considered to have 'entered' a confined space?
options: Only when work actually starts inside
Only after passing 1 m beyond the manway
Only when the whole body is inside the space
When any part, even just the head, is inside
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: confined space entry covers complete body entry and also when only the head is inserted.

q: Which sign is displayed at an approved confined space entry point while the standby person is present?
options: Red: no entry to this confined space at all
Yellow: caution, gas testing now in progress
Blue: breathing apparatus must be worn inside
Green: entry allowed with permit and standby
source: Cl. 5.4: 'ENTRY ALLOWED WITH PERMIT IN THE PRESENCE OF STANDBY PERSON' (green background, white font) at approved entry points.

q: How often must a Confined Space Entry Certificate be re-endorsed?
options: Only at change of work party
source: Cl. 5.4: the Confined Space Entry Certificate must be re-endorsed by each shift.

q: Before personnel enter a vessel, how must it be isolated from connected lines?
options: Stopping, locking and tagging the feed pump
Closing the nearest block valve and tagging it
Closing two valves and opening the bleed between
Spool removal or rated spades near the vessel
source: Cl. 5.2.1: isolation as close as possible to the vessel by physical disconnection or spades/spectacle blinds of the same pressure rating as the flange.

q: During atmospheric venting of a vessel, H2S in the workers' breathing zone exceeds 10 ppm. What must be done?
options: Move workers 5 m away and continue
Issue escape sets and continue venting
Continue venting at a slower rate
Stop venting and remove the source first
source: Cl. 5.2.2: if H2S exceeds 10 ppm in the breathing zone, stop venting and flush/purge or eliminate the source before resuming.

q: Why is a probe extension used when testing the atmosphere inside a vessel after opening the manway?
options: To keep the gas detector sensors dry
To sample inside, not just near the entry
To raise the detector's alarm set points
To test the air just outside the vessel
source: Cl. 5.3: a probe extension shall be used so that the atmosphere within the vessel is sampled and not the region close to entry.

q: What respiratory protection is required to enter a vessel that still contains sludge or residue?
options: SCBA or airline unit at all times
None if the gas test is satisfactory
source: Table 1 Note 2: entry into a vessel having sludge or residue shall be permitted only wearing SCBA / airline unit all the time.

q: Which equipment shall NOT be used for initial air purging of a vessel that contained hydrocarbons?
source: Cl. 5.2.5: electrically driven air movers shall not be used for initial air purging; only at a later stage after gas tests confirm.

q: For welding or cutting inside a confined space, where must compressed gas cylinders be kept?
options: Inside, secured to the vessel wall
Inside, if fitted with flashback arrestors
source: Cl. 5.8: compressed gas cylinders shall not be allowed in a confined space for welding or cutting activities.

q: What must the standby person do each time personnel enter or leave the vessel?
options: Record it at the end of the shift
Inform the Fire Station by phone
Inform the Control Room by radio
Tell the Permit Issuer in person
source: Cl. 5.11: the standby person informs the Control Room by radio each time the vessel is entered or vacated; logged in the Control Room logbook.

q: Entrants must wear SCBA because hydrocarbons are present inside a vessel. Which tools may they use?
source: Cl. 5.7: if SCBA is required due to hydrocarbons, no electrical tools; only pneumatically driven tools; no spark-generating tools.

q: How must pyrophoric sludge be handled during vessel cleaning?
options: Scraped out dry using steel tools
Allowed to dry fully before removal
Left in place until the shutdown ends
Kept wet and removed as soon as possible
source: Cl. 5.10: pyrophoric sludge shall be kept wet and taken out of the vessel as soon as possible and disposed of safely.

q: Why must entrants into a sewer wear SCBA or an airline unit at all times?
options: Sewers have no means of exit
Gas detectors do not work in sewers
Sewers can rarely be fully isolated
source: Table 1 Note 3: sewers rarely can be completely isolated; the atmosphere may pose unpredictable toxic or flammable hazards.

q: On a bench-mounted grinder, what is the maximum gap permitted between the work rest and the abrasive wheel?
source: Cl. 5.1.2.1: work rest adjusted as close to the wheel as possible at a maximum distance of 1/4 inch.

q: The 'ring test' described in KOC.SA.012 for checking an abrasive wheel for cracks is applicable to which type of wheel?
options: Small wheels of 100 mm diameter or less
source: Cl. 5.1.2.3 / 5.1.2.5: the ring test is used only for vitrified bonded wheels; it is not practicable for small, mounted, segment or plate-mounted wheels.

q: After a new abrasive wheel is mounted, how long should it be allowed to run free, with users standing clear, before use?
source: Cl. 5.1.2.3: new wheels should be allowed to run free for about 60 seconds; users should stand clear.

q: A technician is selecting a cutting disc for a portable grinder. Which speed rating requirement must the disc meet?
options: Rated at or above the RPM of the grinder
Rated at 75% of the grinder RPM
Rated below the grinder RPM to reduce vibration
Any rating, provided a speed governor is fitted
source: Cl. 5.1.2.1: ensure speed of the wheel is compatible with the machine, i.e. use a wheel or disc rated at or above the RPM of the grinder.

q: Under KOC.SA.012, a mobile air compressor may be deployed in a Zone 2 hazardous area only:
options: Under a Cold Work Permit with continuous gas monitoring
Under a Hot Work Permit, if suitable for the area classification
Under a Vehicle Entry Permit, if a spark arrestor is fitted
It is never permitted in a Zone 2 area
source: Cl. 5.2.2: mobile compressors are not permitted in Zone 0 & 1; in Zone 2 they must be covered by an authorized Hot Work Permit, subject to suitability.

q: Which method of connecting a pneumatic tool to its high-pressure air hose is acceptable under KOC.SA.012?
options: Screw-adjusted 'Jubilee' clip, tightened with a screwdriver
Crowfoot coupling with retaining pin/clip and whip check
Wire-twisted joint secured with heavy-duty insulation tape
Push-fit coupling, with the hose tied to the tool handle
source: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3: purpose-made connections (e.g. crowfoot) with retaining pin/clip and whip; 'Jubilee' type connections are not permitted.

q: At or above what noise level from air compressors and pneumatic tools must warning signs be displayed and hearing protection worn?
source: Cl. 5.2.1: if noise levels are at or above 85 dB, signs must be displayed and hearing protection worn.

q: Abrasive wheels in a store have been in stock for more than two years. What does KOC.SA.012 recommend before they are issued?
options: Issue them only for light grinding work
Consult the manufacturer or supplier first
Ring test them all, including resin wheels
Discard them without any further assessment
source: Cl. 5.1.2.7: in case of doubt, or if wheels have been in stock for more than two years, the manufacturer/supplier should be consulted.

q: Under KOC.SA.012, how quickly can a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI) shut off power after a ground fault?
source: Cl. 2.0: a GFCI is designed to shut off power in the event of a ground fault within as little as 1/40 of a second.

q: How is a double-insulated portable electric tool identified?
options: A lightning bolt in a circle
source: Cl. 2.0: double-insulated tools are marked with the double insulation symbol (a square within a square).

q: Which gas must NEVER be used to power pneumatic tools?
options: Compressed air from a plant compressor
Compressed air from a mobile compressor
source: Cl. 5.2.3: never use oxygen in pneumatic tools, as oil and gas pressure friction can cause fire or explosion.

q: Why must instrument air NOT be used to operate pneumatic tools?
options: It is too dry to lubricate the tool
It is always above tool rated pressure
Pressure dips could upset the plant
source: Cl. 5.2.1: instrument air must not be used for pneumatic tools to avoid abnormality or upset in plant condition due to pressure variation.

q: An operator finds that a grinder is defective. What should he do?
options: Tag it 'Defective – Don't Use' and report it
Use it carefully until the job ends
Return it to the store without reporting
Repair it on site with spare parts
source: Cl. 5.1.2.6: remove it from service, tag it 'Defective-Don't USE', and report the problem to the supervisor.

q: How often must the Controlling Team's inspection programme check abrasive wheel equipment?
options: Monthly, plus daily user visual checks
Weekly, with no checks by the users
source: Cl. 5.1.2.6: abrasive wheel equipment subject to a monthly inspection programme; users inspect visually daily before use.

q: Which statement about the trigger of a pneumatic tool is correct?
options: It may be tied down if two people operate it
It must not lock 'on'; dead-man never bypassed
Its dead-man switch may be bypassed if guarded
It may be locked 'on' for long cutting jobs
source: Cl. 5.2.3: only finger-operated switches; the tool must not be usable with the trigger locked; dead-man switch never bypassed.

q: Where must batteries of battery-operated tools NOT be removed or replaced?
source: Cl. 5.3.2: batteries must not be removed / replaced in hazardous areas.

q: Which use of compressed air is prohibited under KOC.SA.012?
options: Running an air impact wrench on bolts
Blowing dust off a person's clothing
Powering an approved portable air pump
Driving an air-powered drill on a job
source: Cl. 5.2.3: compressed air should not be used for cleaning dust from the body; exhaust air directed away from the body.

q: How should organic (resin) bonded abrasive wheels be stored to prevent warping?
options: On edge in a cradle in direct sunlight
Stacked in a damp room to stay soft
Flat on a steel surface, away from heat
Hung on hooks through the centre hole
source: Cl. 5.1.2.7: organic bonded wheels should be laid flat on a horizontal steel surface away from excessive heat and moisture.

q: What should be drained from the air receiver, intercooler and aftercooler at the end of each day?
source: Cl. 5.2.2: at the end of each day, any accumulation of oil and water should be drained from the air receiver, intercooler, aftercooler and supply pipes.

q: What is the correct way to disconnect a portable electric tool from a socket?
options: Switch off at the tool and leave it plugged in
Pull the plug, not the cord
Cut the cord near the plug
source: Cl. 5.3.1: pull the plug, not the cord; pulling the cord causes wear and may cause electric shock.

q: What is the maximum age of a contractor's mobile equipment or heavy vehicle permitted for work in KOC business under KOC.SA.013?
source: Cl. 5.2: contractor mobile equipment / heavy vehicles shall not be older than 20 years, subject to suitability and 3rd party certification.

q: How often must a contractor's mobile crane (load handling equipment) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
options: Every 12 months or contract duration, whichever is earlier
source: Cl. 5.4 I a): general mobile equipment once a year (or contract duration if earlier); load or material handling equipment once every 6 months per KOC.SA.029.

q: A contractor's forklift is involved in a minor incident and then repaired. What does KOC.SA.013 require before it is used again?
options: The operator completes a pre-use checklist
A new Clearance Certificate based on a new inspection report
The existing Clearance Certificate is endorsed by the Area HSE Team
No action is needed for a minor incident
source: Cl. 4.6: after any incident or major repair / modification, a new Clearance Certificate is issued based on a new inspection report from a KOC-approved inspection contractor.

q: Under KOC.SA.013, gasoline-operated equipment such as a jumping compactor is restricted on site unless it is fitted with:
options: A reverse alarm and a reverse camera
Vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors
A dead-man switch and emergency stop button
source: Cl. 4.6: gasoline-operated equipment is restricted unless fitted with vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors.

q: In which areas does KOC.SA.013 require mobile equipment to hold a valid Clearance Certificate?
options: Only in Zone 0 and Zone 1 hazardous areas
Only in hazardous areas inside plant fences
In both hazardous and non-hazardous areas
Only for equipment with a State registration plate
source: Cl. 5.1: all mobile equipment shall require a Clearance Certificate for both hazardous and non-hazardous areas including Ahmadi area.

q: A contractor wants to move a generator from Contract A to Contract B, both under the same contractor, using Contract A's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass. Under KOC.SA.013 this is:
options: Acceptable, since the contractor is the same
Acceptable, if the certificate is still valid
Not acceptable; it must be issued under Contract B
source: Cl. 4.6: contractor cannot use mobile equipment with another contract's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass, even if the contractor is the same (drilling teams excepted).

q: During maintenance on a dump truck with a raised bed, which control does KOC.SA.013 require to protect personnel?
options: Lowering the bed onto stacked timber blocks
Fitting a mechanical locking device to the raised bed
Keeping the engine running so hydraulics hold the bed
Posting a banksman to watch the bed during work
source: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): no personnel under a raised bed; use appropriate mechanical locking devices during maintenance to prevent sudden bed movement.

q: Which precaution must be met before a heavy vehicle without an inbuilt spark arrestor is deployed at a KOC worksite?
options: Its exhaust tail pipe must be fitted with a spark arrestor
It must be parked at least 30 m from process equipment
Its engine must be switched off every 30 minutes
Its fuel tank must be at least half full
source: Cl. 5.1.1: the exhaust tail pipe is fitted with a spark arrestor in case it is not inbuilt.

q: How often must general mobile equipment (not load-handling) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
options: Yearly, or contract period if earlier
source: Cl. 5.4 I a): inspection and certification once a year or for the duration of the contract, whichever is earlier (load handling: every 6 months).

q: Under KOC.SA.013, the Security Team issues a Gate Pass for mobile equipment only after it has:
options: A Clearance Certificate from the Controlling Team
A fuel receipt issued by the contractor's office
A verbal OK from the driver's own supervisor
A photograph of the equipment taken at the gate
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4 VI: Security issues the gate pass only after ensuring the equipment has a Clearance Certificate.

q: Which warning device must mobile equipment have to protect people behind it while reversing?
options: A horn fitted on the trailer only
A blue flashing light on the roof
source: Cl. 5.1.1: mobile equipment shall be equipped with a reverse alarm clearly audible to warn persons behind.

q: Besides a reverse alarm, what additional device does KOC.SA.013 require on mobile equipment and heavy vehicles?
source: Cl. 5.1.1: mobile equipment and heavy vehicles shall be equipped with a reverse camera system.

q: During certification, the inspection finds a non-conformance with the Safety Checklist. What concession may the certifying team give?
options: A concession if the contractor signs an undertaking
No concession on any checklist item
A concession for non-critical items only
source: Cl. 5.4 V: certifying teams shall in no case give any concession related to non-conformance on any aspect of the safety checklist.

q: What applies to an in-built non-intrinsically safe radio/music system in a vehicle working in a hazardous area?
options: It may be used if windows are closed
It shall not be switched on or off
It may be used at low volume
It may be used outside Zone 1
source: Cl. 5.1.1: inbuilt non-intrinsically safe transistor / music system shall not be activated (turned on or off).

q: What must be done with an in-built cigarette lighter in mobile equipment before deployment at a KOC worksite?
options: Replace it with a USB charger
Remove it from the power output
Leave it but post a 'No Smoking' sign
source: Cl. 5.1.1: in-built cigarette lighter(s) / any other devices are removed from the power output.

q: Under the 2026 revision, who must the contractor appoint as focal point for maintenance, repairs and operators' equipment concerns?
source: Cl. 4.6: contractor shall assign an Equipment Coordinator responsible for prompt maintenance and repairs and as focal point for operators.

q: When must a heavy equipment operator complete the daily operator checklist?
options: Once a week, on the rest day
At the end of each working shift
source: Cl. 4.6: heavy equipment operator to inspect and fill in the daily operator checklist before start of the work.

q: Which of the following mobile equipment requires third-party test certification under KOC.SA.013?
source: Cl. 5.4 II b): equipment fitted with safety valves (e.g. air compressor) requires 3rd party test certification.

q: How long must Clearance Certificates for mobile equipment be retained if there were no incidents?
options: 2 years from the date of expiry
Until the contract is closed out
1 year from the date of issue
source: Cl. 8.0: Clearance Certificates — minimum 5 years from date of expiry if no incidents; otherwise indefinite.

q: During unloading by a dump truck, what control does KOC.SA.013 require around the truck?
options: A banksman standing behind the bed
Only a horn signal before tipping
Workers guiding the load by hand
source: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): establish and maintain a safe exclusion zone during unloading and install proper barricades.

q: In-service flange bolting replacement (hot bolting) is NOT permitted on flanges having fewer than how many bolts?
source: Cl. 5.3: in-service bolt replacement / rework is not permitted on flanges with less than six bolts.

q: Above what line pressure does KOC.SA.015 prohibit in-service flange bolting replacement?
source: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on high-pressure lines > 13.6 bar (200 psi) including air, nitrogen and hydrocarbons.

q: A gas line contains 800 ppm of H2S. Under KOC.SA.015, can in-service hot bolting be carried out on it?
options: Yes, if all workers wear SCBA
Yes, if line pressure is first reduced
No, it is in highly sour service
No, any line above 10 ppm is excluded
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.3: highly sour service is > 500 ppm H2S; hot bolting is not permitted on systems in highly sour service.

q: During in-service bolt replacement on a live flange, how many bolts may be slackened at any one time?
options: Up to one quarter of the bolts
source: Cl. 5.3 d): slacken one bolt only; under no circumstances must two bolts be slackened at any one time.

q: When fitting new bolts during in-service bolt replacement (without tensioning equipment), how far may the bolt protrude beyond the nut?
options: No more than two full threads
No more than five full threads
source: Cl. 5.3 h): new bolts should protrude no more than two full threads beyond the nut.

q: While breaking a flange, the crew finds the bolts are badly corroded and will not turn. What is the only acceptable removal method under KOC.SA.015?
options: Gas cutting with an oxy-acetylene torch
Striking the nuts with an iron hammer
source: Cl. 5.4: if bolts are corroded, the only acceptable method is a pneumatic hacksaw; gas cutting (open flame) shall not be used.

q: What is the correct body position and first bolt to loosen when breaking a flange that may still contain pressure?
options: Stand downwind and loosen the bolts nearest to you
Stand upwind and loosen the bolts farthest away from you
Stand directly in front and loosen bolts clockwise
Stand upwind and loosen all bolts evenly at the same time
source: Cl. 5.2 o) / 5.5 a): maintain a safe upwind position and loosen bolts farthest away first so any release sprays away from the worker.

q: Which type of hammer may be used when breaking flanges on lines in hydrocarbon service?
options: Any hammer, if a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.4: do not use an iron hammer in hydrocarbon service because impact will generate sparks; only brass hammers shall be used.

q: What is the minimum number of persons required for a flange break under KOC.SA.015?
source: Cl. 5.2 n): 'Flange Break' is a two-person task; two or more persons work together at all times.

q: Who positively identifies, by suitable tagging, all flanges to be broken during the site survey?
source: Cl. 4.1 / 5.1: the Work Permit Issuer conducts a site survey and positively identifies (by tagging) all flanges to be broken.

q: In-service bolt replacement is NOT permitted on systems operating at which temperatures?
source: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on systems operating below 0°C and in excess of 60°C.

q: Who approves the 'In-Service Flange Bolting Replacement / Rework Request Form' (KOC/IS/01)?
options: Completed by Permit Applicant, approved by Permit Issuer
Completed by HSE Officer, approved by Controlling Team
Completed by Permit Issuer, approved by Asset HSE Team
Completed by the fitter, approved by his own supervisor
source: Cl. 5.3: KOC/IS/01 must be completed by the Permit Applicant and approved by the Permit Issuer.

q: Which bolts must be used when reinstating a flange under KOC.SA.015?
options: Any bolts available in the site store
Machine bolts of any available rating
Bolts and nuts of correct size and rating
source: Cl. 4.2: ensure that machine bolts are not used, rather bolts and nuts of appropriate size and rating are used.

q: A fitter wants to slip a pipe over his spanner for extra leverage on a seized bolt. Under KOC.SA.015 this is:
options: Permitted with a second person holding
Permitted if the pipe is short
Not permitted, due to slippage injury
source: Cl. 5.2 j): modification of tools by using additional pipe / cheater bar for extra leverage is not permitted.

q: During hot bolting, may a corroded bolt be removed by burning or grinding?
options: Yes, under a Hot Work Permit
No, hot cutting is not permitted
Yes, if the line is below 13.6 bar
Yes, with a fire watch present
source: Cl. 5.3: bolt cutting by any hot methods, including burning and grinding, is not permitted during hot bolting operations.

q: After one bolt has been replaced during hot bolting, which bolt should be slackened next?
source: Cl. 5.3 j): proceed to slacken the next bolt diagonally opposite to the one just replaced.

q: A leak occurs while workers wearing breathing air masks are breaking a flange. What should they do?
options: Keep masks on and evacuate per the plan
Tighten the bolts before they leave
Stay at the flange and await orders
source: Cl. 5.2 g): workers must not remove their breathing air mask in case of leak; they must follow the emergency plan.

q: Before loosening any flange bolt, how must line depressurization be confirmed?
options: Tap the pipe and listen for gas
Read the control room pressure only
Ask the operator for verbal confirmation
Crack open a nearby drain, vent or gauge
source: Cl. 5.2 e) / 5.4: depressurization confirmed by crack opening a drain / vent, instrument tapping or pressure gauge.

q: Lines containing hydrocarbons are being re-worked in an area. Under KOC.SA.015, other Hot Work in the same area is:
source: Cl. 5.2 m): no other 'Hot Work' is allowed in the same area where lines containing hydrocarbons are being replaced / re-worked.

q: When may a bolt be completely removed while breaking a flange?
options: After the two top bolts have been slackened
At any time, provided the line is drained
Only when all are slack and the flange is apart
As soon as the first bolt turns freely
source: Cl. 5.4: do not completely remove any bolt until all of the bolts have been slackened and the flange is apart.

q: A leak clamp has been installed on a process line. Within what period does KOC.SA.017 require the original integrity of the line to be restored?
source: Cl. 5.2: all clamps are temporary; appropriate actions shall be taken to restore original integrity within three months.

q: If permanent repair cannot be done within the initial period, a Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting may authorize the clamp for a further maximum of:
source: Cl. 5.2 / 5.3: the Asset Owner may request extension through the Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting for a maximum of six months after the initial three months.

q: How far in advance must the Asset Owner submit a Clamp Extension Request, with valid justification, before the agreed clamp period expires?
source: Cl. 5.4: request shall be submitted at least ten working days prior to exceeding the agreed period; authorization from Group Manager (Ops/GO).

q: Inspection finds that the leak on a pipeline is caused by a crack. What does KOC.SA.017 require?
options: Fit a bolt-on mechanical clamp rated for the MAOP
Fit a sealing band clamp centred on the crack
Do not clamp; replace the cracked spool with new pipe
Fit a split sleeve clamp and de-rate the line
source: Cl. 5.2: if a crack appears on any area of the piping, clamping shall not be used; the cracked portion shall be replaced with a new pipe spool.

q: What pressure capability must a bolt-on mechanical leak clamp have under KOC.SA.017?
options: At least 50% of the line's operating pressure
At least equal to the normal operating pressure only
Capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe
Equal to the hydrotest pressure of the clamp only
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.2: clamp design pressure not less than that of the piping; the clamp must be capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe.

q: When sealing band clamps are used on isolated external corrosion pits, what is the minimum spacing between two such clamps?
options: No two clamps within one pipe diameter of each other
No two clamps within 0.5 m of each other
No two clamps within three pipe diameters of each other
No minimum spacing applies between clamps
source: Cl. 5.2: no two such clamps shall be installed within one pipe diameter of each other.

q: When a pipeline leak occurs at a KOC facility, to whom must it be reported in the first instance under KOC.SA.017?
options: Asset PSM Team within 10 working days
Contracts Group through the Clamp Register
source: Cl. 5.1: whenever a leak occurs it shall be reported to ERCU at 160 and all concerned per KOC.GE.007.

q: A pipeline leak is caused by general corrosion and shows signs of multiple leaks. Which repair means should be considered first?
options: A sealing band clamp at each leak point
Epoxy wrap over the corroded area
A bolt-on clamp on the largest leak only
source: Cl. 5.2: clamps are for localized pitting leaks; for general corrosion with multiple leaks, a split sleeve clamp should be considered first.

q: How must a pipeline operating with a leak clamp in position be regarded?
options: As fully repaired and safe to operate normally
As permanently restored once 3 months pass
As under repair; operating it is a last option
As safe, if the clamp is rated for the MAOP
source: Cl. 1.0: clamped piping shall be considered as under repair, regarded as unsafe; operating with a clamp is a last option.

q: Within how many working days must Operations inform Maintenance, HSE, PSM and I&C teams of a leak incident?
source: Cl. 4.1: inform all concerned teams about the leak incident within ten working days from the date of leak.

q: How often must the Clamp Register be updated through joint site inspections and circulated?
source: Cl. 4.1: maintain and update the clamp register monthly through joint site inspections and circulate monthly.

q: How often is the summary report of clamp status in each facility released to PSM, HSE, Maintenance and I&C teams?
source: Cl. 4.1 / 4.6: release the quarterly report of clamp status in each facility (Appendix III).

q: For a sealing band clamp on an isolated corrosion pit, what minimum remaining wall thickness is required within one pipe diameter of the pit?
source: Cl. 5.2: no portion within the one-diameter region shall have minimum remaining wall thickness less than 20% of nominal.

q: How should a clamped location on an underground pipeline be managed after clamping?
options: Left exposed where possible and barricaded
Painted and buried with a marker post
Covered with steel plates and left
source: Cl. 5.5: clamped underground locations shall not be backfilled if possible; exposed locations barricaded with warning signs.

q: Who authorizes a clamp to remain beyond the agreed period, after a Clamp Extension Request meeting?
source: Cl. 5.4: authorization for the extension shall be taken from the Group Manager (Ops/GO).

q: On which pipework shall clamps NOT be installed?
options: Pipe with a single isolated pit
Water lines with a pinhole leak
source: Cl. 5.2: clamps shall not be installed on severely deformed or corroded (externally) piping / pipelines.

q: A clamp has passed the end of its approved extension period. How is it classified?
source: Cl. 5.4 Note: if a clamp exceeds the extension period, it is considered an overdue clamp.

q: Which team issues recommendations (Inspection Action Report) for permanent repair of a leaked pipeline?
source: Cl. 4.2: Inspection & Corrosion Teams issue recommendations (Inspection Action Report or Memorandum) for permanent repairs.

q: Which team is responsible for selecting and installing the approved leak clamp?
source: Cl. 4.3: Maintenance / Gas Maintenance responsible for selection and installation of the approved clamp.

q: If a clamped line must be operated at de-rated parameters, which procedure must be followed?
source: Cl. 5.5: de-rated parameters shall be implemented through the Management of Change Procedure KOC.GE.006.

q: What minimum horizontal radius of warning barricade does KOC.SA.019 require around a hot-tapping site?
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xxii: hot-tapping site shall have a warning barricade with a horizontal radius not less than 15 m; mobile equipment kept upwind outside it.

q: When a line packer or seal plug is used, how must the end of its vent pipe be arranged?
options: At least 15 m away and left open to atmosphere
At least 30 m away and dipped in a water bucket
At least 30 m away and connected to the flare
At least 50 m away and fitted with an end cap
source: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3.3: vent pipe end kept at least 30 m away, dipped in a bucket of clear water, monitored continuously; stop work if bubbles appear.

q: Under KOC.SA.019, for which activity is the signature of the KOC Inspection Engineer required on the work permit?
options: All hot-tapping, welding and plugging work
source: Cl. 4.2: Inspection Engineer approval is required only for in-service welding, after confirming remaining wall thickness.

q: How should the hot-tapping machine be installed with respect to the operator's position?
options: So the operator stands downwind of the machine
So the operator stands upwind of the machine
So the operator stands directly above the cutter
Wind direction is not a consideration
source: Cl. 4.4: ensure the hot-tapping machine is installed in such a way that the operator is positioned in the upwind direction.

q: How must the weight of the hot-tapping machine be managed during the operation?
options: Rest fully on the pipeline being tapped
Be independently supported off the pipeline
Be held by a crane throughout the operation
Be supported on scaffolding tied to the pipe
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xix: the hot-tapping machine shall be independently supported; its weight shall not be transferred to the equipment being tapped.

q: Which statement about sparking tools is correct under KOC.SA.019?
options: They are prohibited during both hot-tapping and welding
They are allowed during hot-tapping but not during welding
They are not allowed during hot-tapping but are allowed during welding
They are allowed during both if a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xviii: sparking tools shall not be used during hot tapping; however, they are allowed during welding.

q: During a plugging operation, which step is designated a 'HOLD POINT' to be witnessed by the Company's representative?
source: Cl. 5.3.3: installation of the gas plug shall be a 'HOLD POINT' witnessed by the Company's representative.

q: During hot-tapping, a leak develops at the machine flange. What must the Worksite Supervisor ensure first?
options: Retrieve the cutter, close the valve and stop safely
Continue cutting at reduced speed to finish the bore
Tighten the flange bolts while the machine is running
Have the fire watch spray the flange and continue
source: Cl. 4.4: if any hazardous situation (e.g. leak) is observed, ensure the cutter is retrieved, the isolation valve closed and hot work stopped safely.

q: Under which type of work permit must hot-tapping be carried out?
source: Cl. 5.1: in-service welding, hot-tapping and plugging must be under the control of a Hot Work Permit.

q: What is 'hot-tapping' as defined in KOC.SA.019?
options: Cutting into live equipment via a fitting
Welding a patch on a depressurized line
Cutting threads into a cold pipe end
Heating a pipe to free a seized valve
source: Cl. 2.3: creating an opening on in-service equipment by cutting or drilling within an attached fitting using a hot-tap machine.

q: When endorsing a permit for in-service welding, what must the Inspection Engineer record?
options: Expected duration of the welding job
Number of fire extinguishers at site
Welder's name and KOC ID number
Wall thickness, MAOP and flow limits
source: Cl. 4.2: mention minimum metal thickness obtained, maximum allowable operating pressure and flow requirements permitted during welding.

q: Under what weather conditions is hot-tapping NOT carried out unless approved by KOC with an enclosure?
options: High wind, storm, dust or rain
source: Cl. 5.3.1 i: hot-tapping shall not be carried out during high windy, stormy, dusty and wet conditions unless approved with a covered enclosure.

q: What fire watch arrangement does KOC.SA.019 require during hot-tapping?
options: None if the gas test reads 0% LEL
A fire watch during night work only
The welder watches for fire himself
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xvi: a dedicated fire watch shall be established and equipped with a suitable extinguisher or pressurized fire hose.

q: What gas monitoring must be specified in the work permit for hot-tapping?
options: Monitoring only if a leak is suspected
One test at the start of the shift
source: Cl. 4.3: gas test before commencement; continuous gas monitoring shall be specified in the work permit.

q: Which communication must be available between the Worksite Supervisor and Operations during hot-tapping?
options: Two-way radio to the control room
Hand signals from the work site
source: Cl. 4.4: two-way radio communication shall be made available between Worksite Supervisor and Operations in the control room.

q: When may the hot-tapping machine be removed after completing the tap?
options: At the end of the working shift, as normal
After the checklist is completed and agreed
Immediately after the cutting is finished
As soon as the fire watch has left the site
source: Cl. 5.4: the machine shall not be removed until the required checklist is completely filled and agreed by KOC concerned teams.

q: Hot-tapping is to be done in an underground access pit. Which additional procedure applies?
source: Cl. 5.3.1 xi: KOC.SA.007 shall be followed; personnel should be equipped with a retrieval system.

q: How must the operating pressure and temperature of the line compare with the hot-tapping machine rating?
options: Only pressure must be within rating
They must never exceed its ratings
They may exceed it if cutting is slow
They may exceed its ratings by 10%
source: Cl. 5.3.2: operating pressure and temperature shall at no time exceed the rated pressure and temperature of the cutting machine.

q: When line packers, seal plugs or expandable plugs are used, which procedure governs the mechanical isolation?
options: KOC.SA.035 Safe Use of Gas Cylinders
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.3.3: mechanical isolation shall be carried out as per KOC.PS.016 when using line packers / seal plugs.

q: Who may carry out hot-tapping work in KOC?
options: KOC-approved contractor or KOC specialist crew
Any welder who holds a valid Hot Work Permit
Operators from the Permit Issuer's own team
Any mechanical contractor working on the site
source: Cl. 4.5: hot-tapping shall be carried out by the KOC approved contractor or the KOC specialized maintenance crew.

q: While welding is in progress, within what radius of the work must the assigned Fire Watch remain until relieved?
source: Cl. 4.5: the Fire Watch shall remain within 8 m radius of the work vicinity during welding / cutting until relieved.

q: After a welding job is completed, how long must the Fire Watch remain at the location?
source: Cl. 4.5: remain at least 30 minutes after hot work until the area is inspected and found free of ignition sources.

q: Before welding in a plant area, flammable materials must be cleared, and drains covered with wet tarpaulins, within what distance of the worksite?
source: Cl. 5.7: flammable materials cleared at least 20 m away; all drains within 20 m covered with wet tarpaulins weighted with sandbags.

q: Under KOC.SA.021, acetylene must not be generated, piped or used at a pressure exceeding:
source: Cl. 5.4: under no condition shall acetylene be used at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge).

q: Why must fittings containing more than 70% copper (other than a burner tip) not be used in acetylene welding equipment?
options: Copper corrodes rapidly in contact with oxygen
Copper and acetylene form explosive copper acetylide
Copper conducts heat back and causes flashback
Copper lowers the flame temperature too much
source: Cl. 5.2: copper in contact with acetylene is liable to form a dangerous explosive compound, copper acetylide.

q: Which filter lens shade range does KOC.SA.021 specify for electric arc welding?
source: Cl. 5.3 Lens Shade Guide: arc welding 10–14; torch brazing 3–4; gas welding 4–8; cutting 3–6.

q: What minimum distance must an electric arc welding generator be kept from the hot work area?
source: Cl. 5.5: the welding generator should be kept at least 5 m away from the hot work area.

q: A pipe must be cold cut inside a hazardous area. Which equipment is permitted under KOC.SA.021?
options: Pneumatic cold cutting machine or manual cutter
Abrasive disc cutter with a spark guard
Any cutter, provided a fire watch is present
source: Cl. 5.6: in a hazardous area only pneumatic cold cutting machines and manual cutters are allowed; electric-driven cutting machines are not allowed.

q: Which coverall is mandatory for all welding and cutting jobs under KOC.SA.021?
source: Cl. 5.3: Inherently Flame Resistant (IFR) coverall with suitable aprons, sleeves and leggings is mandatory for all welding and cutting jobs.

q: What must welders NOT wear while welding?
options: Helmet with an auto-dark filter lens
source: Cl. 5.2: welders should not wear metallic jewelry, rings, or watchstraps.

q: What is the explosive range of acetylene in air stated in KOC.SA.021?
source: Cl. 5.4 / 5.7: explosions are possible from 2% by volume up to 82% acetylene in air.

q: Under KOC.SA.021, the deployment of welding equipment mounted on mobile trucks is:
options: Allowed with a Vehicle Entry Permit
Allowed if the engine is stopped
source: Cl. 5.4: the deployment of welding equipment mounted on mobile trucks is prohibited in all areas.

q: An arc welding generator should have an automatic voltage regulator to reduce the open-circuit voltage to a safe limit, normally about:
source: Cl. 5.5: the arc welding generator should include an automatic voltage regulator reducing open circuit voltage to a safe limit, normally 15 volts.

q: A welding cable is too short. How may two lengths be joined?
options: With a splice wrapped in insulating tape
With standard plug and socket couplers
By twisting the bare cores together
With a screw-type jubilee hose clip
source: Cl. 5.5: if joints are necessary, standard plug and socket couplings shall be used; splices are not allowed in welding cables.

q: Where should an electrode holder be placed when not in use?
options: On a wooden rest, not on the ground
On the ground beside the welder
On the steel structure being welded
Hanging by its cable from the work piece
source: Cl. 5.5: the electrode holder should not be placed on the ground; wooden rests should be provided.

q: Where must an arc strike or test be carried out?
source: Cl. 5.5: in no case shall an arc strike / test be conducted on the equipment or structure; it shall be conducted on test plates.

q: When may an engine-driven welding machine be refuelled?
options: While running, if the welder stops welding
Any time, if a fire extinguisher is nearby
Only when it is not in operation
source: Cl. 5.5: any engine driven welding machine shall not be refuelled while in operation.

q: Under KOC.SA.021, what can a gas plug be relied on for when preparing a pipe for welding?
source: Cl. 5.1: a gas plug will not be considered positive isolation for retaining liquid or pressure, but can be used for sealing off vapours only.

q: Welding is to be done 3 m above ground. What access does KOC.SA.021 require?
options: A stepladder held by a helper
A ladder lashed to the pipe
source: Cl. 5.2: where welding is above 1.8 m, proper scaffolding shall be provided per the Working at Height Procedure.

q: Before cutting the bottom of a tank, what must be done?
options: Cut a small pilot hole with a torch
Paint the cut line with primer
Drill test holes and gas test below
Flood the tank up to the cut level
source: Cl. 5.2: before cutting the bottom of any tank, test holes must be drilled and gas tests carried out.

q: How should ventilation be provided when welding inside a confined space?
options: Natural ventilation through the manway only
Opening an oxygen cylinder valve inside
Blowing compressed oxygen into the space
source: Cl. 5.8: ventilation by extraction fans or air movers rather than blowing fresh air in; compressed oxygen shall never be used.

q: Under the KOC multi-lock sequence for electrical isolation, who applies the FIRST lock?
options: The Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
The Authorized Electrical Person, after confirming isolation
The Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
The Shift Controller, after approving the request
source: Cl. 5.6 (i): the first lock shall be applied by the Authorized Electrical Person immediately after confirming electrical isolation.

q: On completion of work, what is the correct order for removing locks from the multi-lock device before electrical de-isolation?
options: Electrical Person, then Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor
Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor, then Electrical Person
Worksite Supervisor, then Permit Issuer, then Electrical Person
Shift Controller removes all locks together at one time
source: Cl. 5.6: the sequence is reversed for removal — Worksite Supervisor / Permit Applicant first, Permit Issuer second, Authorized Electrical Person last.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered an energy isolating device under KOC.SA.022?
options: A cut-out fuse on the supply circuit
source: Cl. 2.0: push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices.

q: Why does KOC.SA.022 state that Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) should not be used as the point of disconnection?
options: They trip too easily under normal load
Positive contact separation cannot be confirmed
They cannot be fitted with any warning tag
They are only rated for very low voltages
source: Cl. 5.1 f): do not use MCBs as disconnections because confirming positive contact separation is generally not possible.

q: For multi-disciplinary jobs, KOC.SA.022 recommends colour-coded padlocks. Which colour is assigned to Operations?
source: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

q: What is the minimum number of individually marked key storage boxes each facility must have for multi-lockout keys?
source: Cl. 5.7: each facility shall have at least 4 key storage boxes (Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation & Operation).

q: An urgent electrical isolation is needed to protect the plant and workforce. Under KOC.SA.022, how may it be authorized?
options: Verbally by the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller
Only after a written Electrical Isolation Certificate is approved
Verbally by any Worksite Supervisor who is present at site
Only by the Asset HSE Team after carrying out a site visit
source: Cl. 5.4: emergency isolation can be carried out immediately by verbal approval of the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller; written formalities completed once the emergency is over.

q: After isolating and locking an electrical motor, how must the absence of voltage be confirmed before work starts?
options: By pressing the local start button to check it does not run
By testing with an appropriate and tested voltage tester
By checking the breaker indicator light is off
By confirming with the Control Room Operator by radio
source: Cl. 4.4 / 5.1 j)–k): verify isolation by electrical measurement; presence of voltage must be tested using an appropriate and tested voltage tester.

q: In the multi-lock sequence, who applies the SECOND lock?
options: Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
source: Cl. 5.6 (ii): the 2nd lock shall be applied by the Asset Owner (Permit Issuer) prior to issuance of the Work Permit.

q: Who applies the THIRD lock on the multi-lock device?
options: Shift Controller, at the next shift change
Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
Permit Issuer, just before issuing the permit
source: Cl. 5.6 (iii): the 3rd lock shall be applied by the Worksite Supervisor or Permit Applicant after receiving the work permit.

q: In the recommended KOC colour coding, which discipline uses a BLACK padlock?
source: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

q: Who authorizes an Authorized Electrical Person in writing?
options: Asset HSE Team Leader of the area
Permit Issuer of the operating area
source: Cl. 2.0: an Authorized Electrical Person is authorized in writing by the respective area Snr. Engineer Electrical.

q: Which instruction is typical on an electrical tag-out sign?
source: Cl. 5.1 / 5.2: tags convey clear instructions such as 'Do Not Start', 'Do Not Energize' or 'Do Not Operate'.

q: How long must the Electrical Isolation / De-isolation Logbook be retained?
source: Cl. 8.0: Electrical Isolation / De-isolation Logbook — 5 years.

q: During isolation, what must be done about stored electrical energy in batteries and capacitors?
options: Leave it, as it is harmless
source: Cl. 5.1 g): release or render safe all stored or residual energy; stored energy discharged, taking care with batteries and capacitors.

q: What marking must a LOTO padlock carry so it can be recorded on the Isolation Certificate?
source: Cl. 5.2 e): padlock should have a duly imprinted number for record in the Isolation Certificate.

q: According to KOC.SA.022, a 'Danger Notice' indicates a hazard that if not avoided could result in:
source: Cl. 2.0: Danger Notice — could result in death or serious injury; Caution Notice — minor or moderate injury.

q: At a project site outside KOC facilities, who approves a contractor's electrical isolation request after review by the contractor's electrical engineer?
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.1: request reviewed by contractor electrical engineer / supervisor and approved by the KOC representative at site.

q: Before an isolated machine is re-energized, what must be done first?
options: Ask the operator to start it locally
Switch on and watch for sparks
source: Cl. 5.3: clear tools and materials from the machine and clear employees from the area before removing locks and energizing.

q: Under what condition may the Control Room Operator (Operator-I) request an electrical isolation for operational need?
options: At any time, without any approval
Only during the day shift hours
source: Cl. 4.5–4.6: Operator-I can request isolation only with due approval from the Shift Controller; recorded in the Operator-I logbook.

q: According to the KOC.SA.024 JSA flow, who initiates, reviews and authorizes a JSA, respectively?
options: Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer, HSE Team
Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer
Safety Officer, Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant
Permit Issuer, Permit Applicant, Worksite Supervisor
source: Cl. 5.9 / Appendix 1: JSA initiated by Worksite Supervisor, reviewed by Permit Applicant, authorized by Permit Issuer.

q: For which activities does KOC.SA.024 require a JSA WITH Task Risk Assessment (initial and residual risk)?
source: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: JSA with Task Risk Assessment will be carried out only for critical activities.

q: A contractor submits a JSA copied from a similar job at another gathering centre. Under the 2025 revision of KOC.SA.024, this is:
options: Acceptable if the Permit Issuer signs it
Prohibited; a task-specific JSA is needed
Acceptable if reviewed at the toolbox talk
source: Cl. 5.1 Note: the use of generic JSA is strictly prohibited; a standalone JSA specific to the exact task, location and worksite conditions must be developed.

q: In KOC.SA.024, 'residual risk' is best defined as the risk:
options: Present before any controls are applied
Remaining after controls have been applied
Linked to the worst credible outcome only
Accepted by the Permit Issuer without controls
source: Cl. 2.0: residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been applied to associated hazards that have been identified.

q: What size of Risk Assessment Matrix (Severity vs Likelihood) is used in the current KOC JSA template?
source: Revision 3 Aug 2025 / Appendix 1: RAM changed to 6x6 Severity vs Likelihood to align with KOC.GE.018.

q: When a JSA is prepared for a job that involves the use of chemicals, what should it include?
options: A review of the Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
A medical surveillance record for each worker
source: Cl. 5.5: JSAs for jobs that involve the use of chemicals should include a review of SDS sheets.

q: On completion of a job carried out under a work permit, where is the JSA sheet retained as a record?
options: With the Permit Issuer, in file
It is discarded once the permit is closed
source: Cl. 5.7: on completion, the JSA sheet shall be retained in file with the Permit Issuer (routine work without permit: with the Controlling Team).

q: A Task Risk Assessment shows the residual risk remains in the intolerable region and engineering alternatives are not feasible. Under the KOC JSA risk regime, the activity may proceed only:
options: With Manager-level endorsement and a risk-reduction action plan
If the Worksite Supervisor holds an extra toolbox talk on it
If the Permit Issuer marks the permit as a critical activity
If additional PPE is issued to every worker on the task
source: Appendix 1 Risk Control Regime: intolerable risk — activity shall only proceed upon KOC Management endorsement (Manager and above) supported by a detailed action plan.

q: What does a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) do?
options: Records attendance at a toolbox talk
Lists the tools and materials for a job
Calculates the cost and duration of a job
Breaks a job into steps and controls hazards
source: Cl. 2.0: JSA analyzes each job by breaking it into steps, identifying hazards, assessing risk and recommending precautions; also called Job Hazard Analysis.

q: During work under a permit, where must the JSA sheet be kept?
options: At site, with the work permit copy
source: Cl. 4.3 / 5.7: the JSA sheet is kept / attached with the work permit copy at site.

q: How should the Worksite Supervisor brief workers on the JSA before starting work?
options: By e-mail to the whole crew the day before
By giving a copy to the crew foreman only
Through the daily toolbox talk or pre-job meeting
By posting a copy on the camp notice board
source: Cl. 4.3: brief JSA to workers through daily Toolbox Talks / Pre-Job Meeting and ensure all are familiar with it.

q: Which job should be given priority for a JSA under KOC.SA.024?
options: A routine task with no incident history
A task covered by an approved SOP
A new job not done before
source: Cl. 5.1: priority includes new jobs, modified jobs, infrequently performed jobs, potential for severe injury and incident history.

q: How is the Task Risk Assessment carried out for a critical activity?
options: Assessed before and again after controls
Assessed only by the Asset HSE Team
Assessed only for the riskiest step
source: Cl. 5.4: TRA considers initial and residual risks in two steps — before and after application of control measures.

q: Which group conducts periodic audits of JSA procedure compliance in each directorate?
source: Cl. 4.5: the corporate HSE Group is responsible to conduct periodical audit verifying compliance with the JSA Procedure.

q: Which event requires an existing JSA to be modified?
options: Each time a new worker joins the crew
Only after an HSE audit finds a gap
A change in procedure, equipment or process
Only once a year on a fixed review date
source: Cl. 5.8: in case of procedural change, equipment upgrade, change in job or process, JSA will be modified.

q: At shift change, what must the Permit Issuer do with the JSA before endorsing the permit?
options: Nothing; JSA review is only at issue
Send it to the HSE Group
Discard it and issue a new one
source: Cl. 4.2: the Permit Issuer will also review JSA prior to endorsing the permit on shift change.

q: In KOC.SA.024, 'likelihood' is defined as:
options: The cost of controls for the hazard
The degree of harm if it occurs
The expected probability of an event
source: Cl. 2.0: Likelihood — a measure of the expected probability or frequency of an event's occurrence.

q: How is the risk rating obtained in a KOC Task Risk Assessment?
options: By the number of workers involved
By counting the number of hazards
By the length of the job
source: Cl. 2.0: the risk rating is calculated by comparing severity and likelihood of the event's occurrence.

q: Which of the following is a KOC Life Saving Rule printed on the JSA template?
options: Attend the weekly site safety meeting
Obtain authorization before confined space entry
Carry your company ID card at all times
Always work in pairs during the night shift
source: Appendix 1, Section A: Life Saving Rules include 'Obtain Authorization before entering a Confined Space'.

q: When does the Asset / Directorate HSE Team take part in a Task Risk Assessment?
options: For every routine job without exception
Only after an incident has occurred
Never; TRA is for operations only
When the Controlling Team requests support
source: Cl. 4.4: ensure HSE Team participation in the Task Risk Assessment when support is requested from the Controlling Team.

q: During excavation in an EOD-certified area, a worker uncovers a suspected unexploded shell. What is the correct sequence of first actions?
options: Lift it out carefully and carry it away from the trench
Leave it untouched, clear and mark the area, move away, call 160
Photograph it close up on a mobile phone and send it to HSE
Cover it with sand and carry on in another part of the trench
source: Cl. 5.2.4: do not touch; stop work and clear area; mark location at a safe distance; move away before using radio/phone; inform Fire Station / 160; request EOD assistance.

q: Before electric shot firing with electric detonators, all radio communication equipment within what range must be switched off?
source: Cl. 5.1.3.3: handheld radios / transmitters not within 150 m; all radio equipment within 150 m switched off before electric shot firing.

q: A charge fired by safety fuse has misfired. What is the minimum time before anyone may approach it?
source: Cl. 5.1.3.2: no one should approach until not less than 30 minutes (safety fuse) or 10 minutes (electric firing) has elapsed.

q: Under KOC.SA.025, no naked flame, spark or source of ignition is permitted within what distance of an explosive storage facility?
source: Cl. 5.1.1.2: any naked flame, spark or source of ignition shall not be permitted within 25 m (80 ft) of the explosive storage facility.

q: As a minimum, how far must a permanent explosive storage facility be located from any other building or place visited by employees or the public?
source: Cl. 5.1.1.1: permanent explosive storage must be at least 100 m from any other building, habitation or place liable to be visited.

q: Which arrangement for transporting explosives and detonators to a well site complies with KOC.SA.025?
options: Both in the same vehicle, in separate compartments
Both in the same container, if detonators are shunted
In separate vehicles, with no explosives in the driver's cab
Detonators in the driver's cab, explosives in the cargo bed
